why: The only token that distinguishes a plural entry from a singular one in a PO catalog. It cannot appear by accident.
The indexed forms themselves.

The call site, in any of gettext's four plural spellings. WEAK, not strong: a call site is CODE that renders text, and its arguments are often variables — `ngettext(singular, plural, n)` has nothing to translate. Only a locator pointing at TEXT can accuse the engine of missing a string.
A template-level plural. Lives in `.html`, which DOES have an extractor — so a hit here is as likely to be a precision question as a recall one.
Android's resource form.
The call sites, including Compose's. WEAK for the same reason as gettext's: the string lives in a resource file, not here.
Apple's plural dictionary keys.
Xcode 15 String Catalogs.
Any localized string, plural or not. Weak on purpose: it nominates files, it does not accuse them.
Fluent's default-variant marker, which nothing else writes.
Qt's plural element. Its file extension is `.ts`, which this engine hands to the TypeScript grammar.
An ICU plural argument.
Only meaningful inside a plural argument, and it points at a skeleton rather than at a branch body.
Four consecutive pipes. Rare enough elsewhere to be strong.

Symfony's unbounded interval. Specific enough to stand alone; the `{n}` explicit-index half was split off below after it matched a regex alternation `(Jan|Feb|…)` preceded by `{2}` in a repository with no i18n at all.

Symfony's `{0} … |{1} …` form. WEAK, and requiring a second selector after the pipe, because `{2}` is also a regex quantifier and `|` is also a regex alternation — the combination is exactly what a date-parsing regex looks like.
vue-i18n's plural call. Weak: `tc` is a common abbreviation.
A category-suffixed key, scoped to bundle directories so an ordinary object key is not accused.
A category as a child key. Weak because `other` is a word people use for other things.
Nominates the files an i18n runtime touches.
Same, at the call site.
The miss that motivated this whole tool.
